Examezy uses AI for the slow parts of an exam: writing the paper, checking the copies, explaining the results. Every AI output is a draft your team can see, edit and approve.

## Questions, answered
All FAQs
What is Examezy? +
Examezy is an online exam and assessment platform for institutes and hiring teams. You create the paper, schedule it, invite or register candidates, proctor it, evaluate it automatically, on screen or with AI, and publish results with reports, all in one place. It's built by the team behind Vacademy.

How many candidates can write at the same time? +
We load-tested the full exam journey on production with 1,000 simultaneous test-takers: zero errors, every attempt submitted and graded. If you plan a bigger single-window event, we'll plan capacity with you.

What happens if a candidate's internet drops? +
Answers are saved on the device and synced to the server. The candidate sees that their answers are safe, submission retries automatically, and an interrupted attempt can be resumed. Starting the test needs a connection.

How does Examezy stop cheating? +
Every online test forces full screen, warns on tab switches and auto-submits on the third, and blocks copy, paste, right-click and text selection. Camera proctoring adds a check-in selfie, face checks on the device, and snapshots at an interval you choose.

How does AI checking work? +
AI reads handwritten copies or typed long answers, marks each answer against a rubric and your model answer, and writes feedback. Handwritten copies come back checked in red pen. Marks are drafts until a teacher reviews and releases them.

Can I use Examezy for pen-and-paper exams? +
Yes. Print the paper in multiple shuffled sets with an answer key, collect answer sheets as PDFs, check them on screen or with AI, and publish results online.

How much does Examezy cost? +
Plans are sized to the number of candidates and exams you run, and AI checking is paid per copy. Book a demo and we'll send a quote for your exam calendar.

Book a demo

Exam screen

## The interface candidates already know
Section tabs, a question palette that shows answered, not answered and marked-for-review, a running timer and a numeric keypad for number answers. It works the way competitive-exam software works, so candidates spend their time on questions, not on the screen.
Optional reading time lets candidates see the paper before the clock starts, the way a paper exam hands out the question booklet a few minutes early.

- Mark for review and come back
- Lock or allow switching between sections
- Rich text and images in questions, options and passages

Timing

## Timers that match how your exam is actually set
Give the whole test one duration, give each section its own clock, or time every question separately. Choose whether the test submits itself at time-out or waits for the candidate.
Exams run in a fixed live window. Mock tests stay open with a fixed duration, and practice tests are untimed, so one platform covers the final exam and every rehearsal before it.

Reliability

## A dropped connection does not drop the answers
Every answer is saved on the candidate's device and synced to the server as they go. If the network blinks, a banner tells them their answers are safe and will be sent when they are back online. Submission retries on its own, and an interrupted attempt can be resumed.
We load-tested the full exam journey on production with 1,000 candidates writing at the same moment: zero errors, every attempt submitted and graded.

- Answers kept on the device until the server confirms
- Automatic retries on submit
- Resume an interrupted attempt

## Everything in online exams
Sections
Each with its own duration, default marks, negative marking and cutoff.

Negative marking
Set the penalty per section; unattempted questions score zero.

Random question order
Shuffle questions within a section so neighbours see different orders.

- Reading time
A timed preview of the paper before the exam clock starts.

Browser restrictions
Full screen, tab-switch warnings, copy and right-click blocked.

Reminders
Starting-soon and started emails, plus WhatsApp through automations.

Instant results
Release on submit, at the end of the window, or when you choose.

Batches or open links
Assign to batches and individuals, or open a public registration page.

## Questions about online exams
How many candidates can take an exam at the same time? +
We load-tested the full exam journey on our production system with 1,000 candidates writing simultaneously on a 30-question paper: zero errors, and every attempt was submitted and graded. If you expect more than that in a single window, tell us during the demo and we will plan capacity with you.

What happens if a candidate's internet drops mid-exam? +
Answers are saved on the device as they are given and synced to the server. The candidate sees a banner saying their answers are safe, submission retries automatically, and an interrupted attempt can be resumed. Starting a test does need a working connection.

Can I time each section separately? +
Yes. Duration can be set for the whole test, for each section, or for each question, and you can allow or block switching between sections.

Does the test submit itself when time is up? +
If you choose auto-submit, yes. You can also let candidates submit themselves.

Can candidates take the exam on a phone? +
Yes, the exam runs in any modern browser on a laptop, tablet or phone. For high-stakes papers we recommend a laptop, since full-screen and tab-switch rules are designed around a desktop browser.

AI proctoring

# Proctoring that catches the obvious, without streaming anyone's bedroom.
Every online test is locked to full screen and watches for tab switches. Turn on camera proctoring and Examezy counts faces on the candidate's own device, takes small snapshots, flags what looks wrong and lets you decide what a flag means.

- Face checks run on the device
- No video streamed
- Auto-submit on the 3rd tab switch
- Snapshot timeline for review

Always on

## Browser rules on every online test
The exam opens in full screen. Leaving the tab triggers a warning; the third switch submits the test automatically. Copying, right-click and text selection are blocked, and paste is blocked in typed answers.
None of this needs a plugin or a special browser, so candidates do not get stuck installing software on exam morning.

- Forced full screen
- Tab-switch warnings, auto-submit on the 3rd
- Copy, paste, right-click and selection blocked

Camera proctoring

## A camera check-in, then quiet watching
Before starting, the candidate sees a live preview and takes a selfie. You can make the camera mandatory: no camera, no exam.
During the exam a face detector runs on the candidate's device. No face for six seconds, or more than one face for a couple of seconds, raises a flag and takes a snapshot. Small JPEG snapshots are also taken at an interval you choose, from every 10 seconds to every 10 minutes.

- Check-in selfie and live preview
- Flags for no face and multiple faces
- Snapshots every 10 s to 10 min, plus one at each flag

Before you start · Camera check-in
Camera required
Face in frame

- Camera allowed
- Selfie captured
- One face detected
Snapshots every 60 s and at each flag. Nothing is streamed.
Start exam

Your rules

## You decide what a flag means
Pick a violation limit of 3, 5 or 10 flags before the test submits itself, or record only and let a teacher judge afterwards. Lost camera, denied camera, full-screen exits and tab switches all land in the same log.
After the exam, open any attempt to see a timeline of events with the snapshots beside them. Review takes minutes, not hours of video.

## Everything in ai proctoring
Light on bandwidth
Only small snapshots travel, so it works on ordinary home connections.

Privacy by design
Faces are counted on the device. Nothing is streamed live.

Event log
Tab switch, full-screen exit, camera lost, no face, multiple faces, auto-submitted.

Per assessment
Off unless you choose it, so practice tests stay friction-free.

Shuffled orders
Random question order per section; shuffled sets for printed papers.

Fails safe
If the camera hiccups, it records less. It never blocks an honest candidate.

## Questions about ai proctoring
Does Examezy record video of candidates? +
No. Faces are detected on the candidate's own device and only small still snapshots are uploaded, at the interval you set and whenever a flag is raised. No video is streamed or stored.

What counts as a violation? +
Switching tabs, leaving full screen, the camera being denied or lost, no face in view for about six seconds, or more than one face in view. Each is logged with a timestamp, and camera flags come with a snapshot.

Will the test be auto-submitted for a violation? +
Three tab switches always submit an online test. For camera flags you choose: auto-submit after 3, 5 or 10 flags, or never, so a teacher reviews the timeline and decides.

Do candidates need to install anything? +
No. Proctoring runs in the browser. Candidates allow camera access when asked, and you can make that mandatory to start.

Is there a lockdown browser or ID verification? +
Not today. Examezy's proctoring is the browser rules above plus camera checks. If you need a lockdown browser or live human invigilators for a certification exam, tell us in the demo and we will be straight about whether Examezy fits.

Objective

## Questions that mark themselves the moment the test ends
Single-correct and multiple-correct MCQs, true/false, numeric answers (single digit, integer, positive integer or decimal, with more than one accepted value if you like) and one-word answers that ignore case and extra spaces.
Negative marking is set per section, and results can reach candidates the second they submit.

- MCQ single and multiple correct
- True / false
- Numeric with several accepted values
- One word, case-insensitive

Coding

## Code that runs, against tests the candidate can't see
Coding questions come with an editor inside the exam. Python and JavaScript run in the browser; C, C++, Java and Go run on a judge server. Marks are proportional to the hidden test cases passed, and scoring is repeated on the server.

Coding · Q2 · Two Sum · Python
Run
1 def two_sum(nums, target):
2 seen = {}
3 for i, n in enumerate(nums):
4 if target - n in seen:
5 return [seen[target - n], i]
6 seen[n] = i
7
Hidden tests

8 / 10 marks
8 of 10 test cases passed
Python JS C C++ Java Go

## Everything in question types
MCQ (single correct)
Full marks for the right option, the section's penalty for a wrong one.

MCQ (multiple correct)
Candidates pick every correct option.

True / false
Quick checks of a concept, auto-marked.

Numeric
Integer, decimal or single-digit answers, several accepted values.

One word
Short typed answers, matched ignoring case and spacing.

Long answer
Teacher-checked, or AI-graded against a rubric.

Coding
Six languages, hidden test cases, proportional marks.

Passage-based
Comprehension versions of MCQ and numeric questions.

## Questions about question types
Which question types are auto-marked? +
Single and multiple-correct MCQs, true/false, numeric, one word and coding are marked automatically. Long answers are checked by a teacher, or by AI against a rubric if you turn AI checking on.

Can a numeric question accept more than one answer? +
Yes, you can list several accepted values. Answers are matched exactly, so for decimals set the precision you expect in the question.

Can I add images and formulas to questions? +
Questions, options, explanations and passages use a rich-text editor with images, so diagrams and figures sit right in the question.

Do you support match-the-following or fill-in-the-blank? +
Not as their own types today. Most institutes set these as MCQs or one-word questions. Tell us if they matter for your papers.

Which languages can coding questions use? +
Python, JavaScript, C, C++, Java and Go.

## Questions about question bank
Can I import my existing question papers? +
Yes. Word documents import with simple markers for questions, options and answers. Printed or scanned papers can be digitised with the AI extractor.

If I edit a question, do old results change? +
Questions are linked into tests with their own marks and order. Talk to us about your editing workflow in the demo; we'll show how reuse and versioning work for your team.

Can several teachers share one bank? +
Yes. The bank belongs to the institute, and per-test access settings control who can create, edit and evaluate each assessment.

Does AI generation use my own material? +
Yes. Generate from your PDFs, Word files, slides or knowledge base. Knowledge-base questions cite the source page so a teacher can check them quickly.

## Questions about paper & offline exams
Does Examezy scan OMR sheets? +
No. Examezy handles written answer sheets: printed papers, uploaded PDFs, on-screen checking and AI checking of handwriting. If you run OMR bubble sheets today, keep your scanner and talk to us about bringing the results into Examezy's reports.

How do students submit a paper answer sheet? +
For remote written tests they download the paper, write on paper and upload one PDF. For hall exams, an admin uploads the scans, one at a time or in bulk with AI matching each copy to its student.

Can AI check handwritten answers? +
Yes. AI checking reads the handwriting, marks each answer against a rubric and returns a red-pen checked copy. Marks stay a draft until a teacher approves and releases them.

Can I enter marks for an exam that was checked by hand? +
Yes, offline result entry lets you enter responses per question or import a ZIP of results, graded by the same engine. It is switched on per institute; ask us during setup.

On-screen marking

## A red pen, without the stack of paper
Evaluators open the answer sheet in the browser and mark it with pen, tick, cross, text, boxes and circles in any colour, with undo and a built-in calculator. Marks are entered per question, kept within each question's maximum, with remarks for the student.
Drafts save as they go. When the evaluator submits, the checked copy is stored and the result released, and the student sees their own marked sheet.

## Questions about evaluation & marking
Can I re-evaluate after fixing an answer key? +
Yes. Re-run evaluation for the whole assessment, for selected participants, or for selected questions of selected participants.

Can several teachers evaluate the same test? +
Yes. Each assessment's access settings decide who evaluates, by role or by named user.

Will AI publish marks without a teacher? +
No. AI marks are drafts. A teacher reviews, edits if needed and releases, and students see nothing before release.

Do students see their checked copy? +
Yes, once the result is released they can see their marked answer sheet alongside their report.

Pay per copy
Cost previewed first; failures free.

## Questions about ai answer-sheet checking
How accurate is AI answer-sheet checking? +
It applies one rubric consistently and handles most legible handwriting, including maths. It can misread messy writing, which is why every mark is a draft a teacher reviews before release. We'll check a few of your own copies in the demo so you can judge.

How long does it take? +
Typically 1 to 8 minutes per handwritten copy and about 20 seconds for typed long answers. Copies are checked in parallel, so a class is usually done in well under an hour.

What does it cost? +
AI checking is paid per copy, based on the number of questions, and the cost is shown before you start. Failed, cancelled and unreadable copies are not charged.

Is this the same as Evalezy? +
Yes, it's the same engine. Evalezy (evalezy.com) is our standalone product and API for teams that only want AI copy checking. Inside Examezy it's part of the full exam workflow.

## Questions about results & analytics
Can students see their rank and percentile? +

Can I download every student's report at once? +

Which export formats are supported? +
CSV and PDF for leaderboards, participant lists and question insights, and ZIP for bulk report PDFs.

Can parents receive results on WhatsApp? +
Result release can trigger WhatsApp, email or push messages through Automations, including rank and percentile. Set the message once and it goes out with every release.

## Questions about open registration tests
Can anyone take an open test without an account? +
Candidates register on the public page and create an account with OTP verification. That's what gives you verified contact details for every test-taker.

Can I collect a registration fee? +
Not inside the test registration today. Most institutes run free scholarship and talent tests as lead magnets. Ask us if fee collection matters for your exam.

Can I add custom questions to the registration form? +
Yes. Add the fields you need, and they appear in participant exports alongside marks, rank and percentile.

Can registrants get reminders on WhatsApp? +
Yes, through Automations: registration, starting-soon, started and result messages by WhatsApp, email or push.

Online exams Timed, sectioned exams that survive a dropped connection. Results & analytics Rank, percentile, question insights, AI reports. AI proctoring On-device face checks, snapshots and auto-submit rules.

# Coding rounds that grade themselves.
Add coding questions to any test. Candidates write and run code inside the exam, marks come from hidden test cases, and the same paper can carry aptitude MCQs and a camera-proctored setting.
Book a demo See how it works

- Python, JS, C, C++, Java, Go
- Hidden test cases
- Marks per test case passed
- Mix with MCQs

Coding · Q2 · Two Sum · Python
Run
1 def two_sum(nums, target):
2 seen = {}
3 for i, n in enumerate(nums):
4 if target - n in seen:
5 return [seen[target - n], i]
6 seen[n] = i
7
Hidden tests

8 / 10 marks
8 of 10 test cases passed
Python JS C C++ Java Go

Write & run

## An editor inside the exam, not a link to another site
Candidates write code in the exam screen and run it against sample cases. Python and JavaScript run right in the browser; C, C++, Java and Go run on a judge server.

- A Python
- B JavaScript
- C C
- D C++
- E Java
- F Go

Grade

## Partial credit that reflects partial solutions
Marks are proportional to the hidden test cases passed, so a solution that handles most cases earns most marks. Scores are recomputed on the server against the test cases you wrote.

## Questions about coding tests
Which programming languages are supported? +
Python, JavaScript, C, C++, Java and Go.

How are coding answers marked? +
Against hidden test cases you write. Marks are proportional to the number of test cases passed, and scoring is repeated on the server.

Can I combine coding with aptitude questions? +
Yes. A test can have an MCQ section and a coding section, each with its own timer.

Do you detect copied code between candidates? +
Not today. Integrity comes from proctoring (camera checks, full-screen and tab-switch rules) and shuffled question order.

Step by step

## The detail behind each step
Every setting below is configurable per assessment, so a weekly quiz and a scholarship test can live side by side with different rules.

- 1 Create the assessment A four-step wizard: basic info (type, window, duration, result release), sections and questions, participants and notifications, and access control. It stays a draft until you publish.
- 2 Add questions Pick from the question bank, import a Word file, digitise a printed paper, or generate with AI from your material. Set marks, negative marking, cutoffs and order per section.
- 3 Choose who takes it Assign batches or individuals, or open a public registration page with your own form, a registration window and OTP verification.
- 4 Set the rules Timers per test, section or question; auto-submit; section switching; full screen and tab-switch limits; camera proctoring with your violation limit.
- 5 Run the exam Candidates write in the browser with autosave. You watch Attempted, Ongoing and Pending live, send reminders and grant reattempts.
- 6 Evaluate Objective answers are marked on submit. Teachers check long answers and uploaded sheets on screen, or review AI-drafted marks.
- 7 Release and analyse Release on submit, at the end of the window or manually. Students get rank, percentile and a detailed report; you get insights, exports and the dashboard.

Online, paper or both

## The same flow, wherever the exam is written
Paper exams follow the same seven steps; the only difference is that answer sheets arrive as scanned PDFs and are checked on screen or by AI.

- Online Paper Hybrid
Written in the browser, marked on submit

- 1 Candidates write on laptop, tablet or phone
- 2 Answers autosave; proctoring rules apply
- 3 Objective answers marked instantly
- 4 Long answers checked on screen or by AI
- 5 Report with rank and percentile

## Online exams

Details

- Sections. Each with its own duration, default marks, negative marking and cutoff.
- Negative marking. Set the penalty per section; unattempted questions score zero.
- Random question order. Shuffle questions within a section so neighbours see different orders.
- Reading time. A timed preview of the paper before the exam clock starts.
- Browser restrictions. Full screen, tab-switch warnings, copy and right-click blocked.
- Reminders. Starting-soon and started emails, plus WhatsApp through automations.
- Instant results. Release on submit, at the end of the window, or when you choose.
- Batches or open links. Assign to batches and individuals, or open a public registration page.

## AI proctoring

Details

- Light on bandwidth. Only small snapshots travel, so it works on ordinary home connections.
- Privacy by design. Faces are counted on the device. Nothing is streamed live.
- Event log. Tab switch, full-screen exit, camera lost, no face, multiple faces, auto-submitted.
- Per assessment. Off unless you choose it, so practice tests stay friction-free.
- Shuffled orders. Random question order per section; shuffled sets for printed papers.
- Fails safe. If the camera hiccups, it records less. It never blocks an honest candidate.

## Question types

Details

- MCQ (single correct). Full marks for the right option, the section's penalty for a wrong one.
- MCQ (multiple correct). Candidates pick every correct option.
- True / false. Quick checks of a concept, auto-marked.
- Numeric. Integer, decimal or single-digit answers, several accepted values.
- One word. Short typed answers, matched ignoring case and spacing.
- Long answer. Teacher-checked, or AI-graded against a rubric.
- Coding. Six languages, hidden test cases, proportional marks.
- Passage-based. Comprehension versions of MCQ and numeric questions.

## Question bank

Details

- Powerful filters. Type, difficulty, subject, tags, date and source.
- Reuse without copying. One question, many tests, each with its own marks.
- Word import. Marker-based import of whole papers.
- Digitise printed papers. Photo or PDF of a paper into editable questions.
- AI generation. From documents, images, audio, topics or your knowledge base.
- Explanations. Add a solution once; candidates see it in their review.

## AI question paper generator

Details

- Up to 120 questions. A full-length paper in one go.
- Cited sources. Page references for knowledge-base questions.
- Print-ready. Download a paper PDF, or run it online.
- Coding questions too. Generate programming problems with test cases.
- Chat to refine. Ask for harder, shorter or more application-based questions.
- Into your bank. Everything generated is saved and tagged for reuse.

## Paper & offline exams

Details

- Print-ready PDF. Sets, keys and header fields.
- PDF answer sheets. Uploaded by the student or by an admin.
- On-screen checking. Pen, tick, cross, text, shapes, calculator.
- AI checking. Handwriting read, marked, checked copy returned.
- Offline result entry. Enter responses or import a ZIP of results (on request).
- One set of reports. Paper and online results side by side.

## Evaluation & marking

Details

- Evaluator access. Choose who evaluates each test, by role or by name.
- Re-evaluation. Whole test, selected candidates or selected questions.
- Evaluation backlog. See what's checked, by whom, and what's waiting.
- Remarks. Feedback per question, visible after release.
- Result holds. Nothing released until you say so.
- Release alerts. Result emails with the report PDF attached.

## AI answer-sheet checking

Details

- 200 copies per upload. PDF scans from any scanner or phone app.
- No guessing. Unmatched copies wait for a teacher.
- Maths-aware. Equations and working read line by line.
- Red-pen copy. Ticks, crosses, notes and the total, on the student's own sheet.
- Minutes, not weeks. Typically 1–8 minutes per handwritten copy.
- Pay per copy. Cost previewed first; failures free.

## Results & analytics

Details

- Leaderboard. Rank, percentile, marks and time; CSV and PDF.
- Overview. Attempted, ongoing, average marks and time.
- Bulk report ZIP. One PDF per student, plus an index.
- AI diagnostics. Misconceptions, topic accuracy, thinking skills.
- Survey reports. Option percentages and free-text answers.
- Result alerts. Release emails with PDF; WhatsApp via automations.

## Open registration tests

Details

- Public link. Share anywhere: ads, WhatsApp groups, school visits.
- Custom form. Ask for exactly the details your team needs.
- OTP verified. Real phone numbers, not fake sign-ups.
- Two windows. Registration window and exam window, set separately.
- Automations. Registration, reminder, start and result messages.
- Rank lists. Leaderboard with percentile, ready for scholarships.

## Coding tests

Details

- Six languages. Python, JavaScript, C, C++, Java, Go.
- Hidden test cases. Candidates can't hard-code the answers.
- Proportional marks. Per test case passed.
- AI-generated problems. Draft new coding questions fast.
- Proctored. Camera checks and browser rules.
- Rank lists. Shortlist straight from the leaderboard.

Assessment types

# Online Exam Software FAQ: Proctoring, Evaluation, Results | Examezy
URL: https://examezy.com/faq/

- Home
- / FAQ
FAQ

# Straight answers about running exams on Examezy.
Proctoring, internet drops, paper exams, AI checking, results, scale and pricing. If your question isn't here, ask us on WhatsApp.
Book a demo See how it works

## The platform
What is Examezy? +
Examezy is an online exam and assessment platform for institutes and hiring teams. You create the paper, schedule it, invite or register candidates, proctor it, evaluate it automatically, on screen or with AI, and publish results with reports, all in one place. It's built by the team behind Vacademy.

What kinds of tests can I run? +
Live exams in a fixed window, self-paced mock tests with a fixed duration, untimed practice tests, surveys, and paper exams where candidates upload their written answer sheet. Tests can also be embedded inside Vacademy courses.

Which question types are supported? +
MCQ with one correct answer, MCQ with multiple correct answers, true/false, numeric, one word, long answer and coding, plus passage-based versions of MCQ and numeric questions. Questions support rich text and images.

Can I import my existing question papers? +
Yes. Import Word documents with simple markers, digitise printed or scanned papers with the AI extractor, or generate new questions with AI from your own material.

Does it work on our own domain and brand? +
Yes, through Vacademy's white-label portals with your domain, logo and colours.

## Exam day
How many candidates can write at the same time? +
We load-tested the full exam journey on production with 1,000 simultaneous test-takers: zero errors, every attempt submitted and graded. If you plan a bigger single-window event, we'll plan capacity with you.

What happens if a candidate's internet drops? +
Answers are saved on the device and synced to the server. The candidate sees that their answers are safe, submission retries automatically, and an interrupted attempt can be resumed. Starting the test needs a connection.

Do candidates need to install anything? +
No. Examezy runs in any modern browser on a laptop, tablet or phone.

Can I watch the exam live? +
Yes. The monitoring console shows who has attempted, who is writing now and who hasn't started, with reminders, reattempts and closing submissions one click away.

Can I give a student a second attempt? +
Yes. Grant a reattempt from the monitoring console. Students can also request one, and requests land in an inbox for you to approve.

## Proctoring
How does Examezy stop cheating? +
Every online test forces full screen, warns on tab switches and auto-submits on the third, and blocks copy, paste, right-click and text selection. Camera proctoring adds a check-in selfie, face checks on the device, and snapshots at an interval you choose.

Is video recorded? +
No. Faces are counted on the candidate's device and only small still snapshots are uploaded. No video is streamed or stored.

Can a candidate be auto-submitted for camera flags? +
If you choose. Set a limit of 3, 5 or 10 flags, or record only and let a teacher review the timeline.

Do you have a lockdown browser or ID verification? +
Not today. Integrity comes from browser rules and camera checks. We'll tell you honestly in the demo whether that's enough for your exam.

## Evaluation & results
Which answers are marked automatically? +
MCQs, true/false, numeric, one word and coding are marked on submit. Long answers and uploaded answer sheets go to teachers, or to AI checking if you turn it on.

How does AI checking work? +
AI reads handwritten copies or typed long answers, marks each answer against a rubric and your model answer, and writes feedback. Handwritten copies come back checked in red pen. Marks are drafts until a teacher reviews and releases them.

What does AI checking cost? +
It's paid per copy based on the number of questions, with the cost shown before you run it. Failed, cancelled and unreadable copies are free.

Can I fix an answer key after the exam? +
Yes. Correct the key and re-evaluate the whole test, selected candidates, or selected questions.

What do students see in their report? +
Score, rank, percentile, comparison with the class average and topper, accuracy and time per section, a question-wise review with explanations, how the class answered each question, their checked copy, and an AI report with strengths, misconceptions and a learning path.

Can I export results? +
Yes: leaderboards and participant lists as CSV or PDF, question insights as PDF, and a ZIP with one report PDF per student.

## Paper exams
Can I use Examezy for pen-and-paper exams? +
Yes. Print the paper in multiple shuffled sets with an answer key, collect answer sheets as PDFs, check them on screen or with AI, and publish results online.

Does Examezy scan OMR sheets? +
No. Examezy works with written answer sheets, not OMR bubble sheets.

How are scanned copies matched to students? +
Upload up to 200 PDFs at once; AI reads the name and roll number on each copy and matches it to your class list. Anything unclear waits for a teacher.

## Buying
How much does Examezy cost? +
Plans are sized to the number of candidates and exams you run, and AI checking is paid per copy. Book a demo and we'll send a quote for your exam calendar.

Can we try it before committing? +
Yes. Send us a past paper and we'll set it up as a test, so you can run a pilot exam with one batch.

How long does setup take? +
You can run a first test as soon as your questions and candidates are in. We help you import your first paper and set it up during onboarding.

Who is behind Examezy? +
Examezy is built by Vidyayatan Technologies, the team behind the Vacademy learning platform.

# Online Exam & Assessment Glossary: 40 Terms Explained | Examezy
URL: https://examezy.com/glossary/

- Home
- / Exam glossary
Exam glossary

# Online exam terms, in plain English.
Forty terms exam heads, teachers and HR teams run into, from answer keys to tab switching, each with a one-line definition.
Book a demo See how it works

A B C D E F H I L M N O P Q R S T A
Answer keyThe list of correct answers for objective questions, used to mark them. A wrong key is fixed by correcting it and re-evaluating. Re-evaluation →
Answer sheetThe paper on which a candidate writes answers in a written exam; in online marking it is scanned into a PDF. Paper exams →
Assertion-reason questionA question pairing a statement with a reason; the candidate chooses whether each is true and whether the reason explains the assertion. Usually set as a single-correct MCQ.
Auto-submitSubmitting a test automatically when time runs out or after a set number of integrity violations. Online exams →

B
Bloom's taxonomyA ladder of thinking skills (remember, understand, apply, analyse, evaluate, create) used to balance a paper beyond recall. AI reports →
BlueprintA table that fixes marks per unit, question type and difficulty before questions are written. Blueprint guide →

C
Comprehension (passage-based) questionQuestions that refer to a shared passage, data set or case study shown alongside them. Question types →
Computer-based test (CBT)An exam taken on a computer rather than on paper, usually in a supervised centre.
CutoffThe minimum marks needed to qualify, set for a whole test or for each section.

D
Diagnostic testA test designed to find gaps in understanding rather than to rank, usually given before teaching.

E
EvaluatorThe person who checks and marks subjective answers. Access to evaluate is usually controlled per exam.

F
Formative assessmentFrequent, low-stakes checks during learning, such as quizzes and practice tests, used to guide teaching.

H
Hidden test casesInputs used to mark a coding answer that the candidate cannot see, so solutions can't be hard-coded. Coding tests →

I
Item analysisStudying each question's results (how many got it right, which wrong options were chosen) to judge its quality and the class's understanding. Question insights →

L
LeaderboardA ranked list of candidates by marks, often with time taken and percentile.
Live windowThe fixed period in which a scheduled exam can be started and written.

M
Marking schemeThe rules for awarding marks: points expected per answer, step marks and penalties.
Mark for reviewA flag a candidate puts on a question to return to it before submitting.
MCQ (multiple choice question)A question with options from which the candidate picks one (single correct) or several (multiple correct) answers.
Mock testA full-length rehearsal of a real exam with the same pattern, timing and marking. Mock test series →
Model answerA teacher's ideal answer to a subjective question, used to guide marking.

N
Negative markingDeducting marks for wrong answers to discourage guessing. Negative marking explained →
Numeric answer typeA question answered by typing a number instead of choosing an option.

O
OMR (optical mark recognition)Reading filled bubbles on printed answer sheets with a scanner. Different from checking written answers on screen.
On-screen marking (OSM)Checking scanned answer sheets on a computer instead of on paper. On-screen checking →
Open registration testA test anyone can register for through a public link, often used for scholarships and admissions. Open registration →

P
PercentileThe percentage of test-takers who scored at or below a given candidate. Rank vs percentile →
Practice testAn untimed, always-open test meant for learning rather than ranking.
ProctoringSupervising an exam to keep it fair, in person or remotely through browser rules and camera checks. AI proctoring →

Q
Question bankA searchable store of questions, tagged by topic, type and difficulty, used to build papers. Question bank →
Question paletteThe grid of question numbers on an exam screen showing which are answered, unanswered or marked for review.

R
RandomisationShuffling question order (or printing different sets) so neighbouring candidates see different papers.
Re-evaluationMarking answers again, for example after a corrected answer key or a candidate's request.
Reading timeA short timed preview of the paper before the exam clock starts.
Remote proctoringProctoring candidates who write from home, using their own device's browser and camera.
RubricA breakdown of what earns marks in a subjective answer, criterion by criterion. AI checking →

S
SectionA part of a paper with its own questions and, often, its own timer, marks and cutoff.
Summative assessmentA test at the end of a unit, term or course that measures what was learned, such as a term exam.

T
Tab switchingLeaving the exam tab for another tab or app, which proctoring tools detect and limit.
Test seriesA planned sequence of tests, usually chapter tests building to full mocks, before a competitive exam.

# Exam Integrity, Security and Privacy on Examezy | Examezy
URL: https://examezy.com/security/

- Home
- / Security & privacy
Security & privacy

# Fair exams, private candidates, results you control.
How Examezy protects exam integrity and candidate privacy, and, just as important, what we don't claim.
Book a demo See how it works

Fair conditions on every test
Online tests open in full screen. Tab switches are warned and the third submits the test. Copy, paste, right-click and text selection are blocked in the exam.

Camera checks without surveillance
When camera proctoring is on, faces are counted on the candidate's own device. Only small still snapshots are uploaded, at the interval you choose and when a flag is raised. No video is streamed or recorded.

Access per assessment
For each test you decide who can edit it, who gets live alerts, who can see submissions and reports, and who evaluates, by role or by named person.

Results held until you release
Results go out on submit, at the end of the window, or only when you release them. AI-drafted marks stay drafts until a teacher reviews them; learners see nothing before release.

Verified candidates on open tests
Candidates on public registration pages create an account and verify their phone by OTP before they can take the test.

## What we don't claim
Security pages are full of badges. Here's what you won't see on ours, so you can plan around it. If your exam needs any of these, ask us before you buy.

- ISO 27001, SOC 2 or similar certifications

- A data-residency guarantee

- A lockdown browser, ID matching against a photo, or live human invigilation

- Detection of phones or other people outside the camera's view

## Privacy for candidates
Tell candidates what you collect and why. With camera proctoring that means a check-in selfie and occasional snapshots; without it, nothing beyond their answers and the events of the attempt (such as tab switches). Examezy is operated by Vidyayatan Technologies LLP under the Vacademy privacy policy .

# About Examezy | Examezy
URL: https://examezy.com/about/

- Home
- / About
About

# Exams made easy, for the people who run them.
Examezy is the exams and assessments platform from the team behind Vacademy. We built it for exam heads, coaching owners, teachers and HR teams who are tired of stitching an exam together from five tools.
Book a demo See how it works

## Why we built it
Every institute we work with runs exams. Most were doing it with a form tool for online tests, Word for papers, a weekend of checking, Excel for rank lists and WhatsApp for results. Each tool is fine; together they cost teachers their evenings and students their feedback.
Examezy puts the whole exam in one place, online or on paper, and uses AI where it saves real hours (writing papers, checking copies, explaining results) while keeping a person in charge of every mark.

## How we work

- We only claim what the product does today. Our home page lists what we don't do yet.
- AI drafts; teachers decide.
- Candidates' privacy is part of fairness: no video streaming, ever.

The family
Vacademy The learning platform: courses, live classes, community. Evalezy AI checking of handwritten answer sheets, with an API. Tutezy A personalised AI tutor for every student. Telleo AI calling for admissions and follow-ups. VoomSales An admissions CRM built for institutes.

Examezy is built by the team behind Vacademy, the learning and assessment platform used by schools, coaching institutes, online academies and training institutes across 5 countries.

For coaching institutes

# A test series your students will measure themselves by.
Weekly tests, full-length mocks, scholarship tests and doubt-clearing reports, run from one platform. Students get rank and percentile minutes after they submit; your faculty get the questions the batch got wrong.
Book a demo See the workflow

- 5 Rohan Gupta 270/300 99.6

Sound familiar?

## What gets in the way today
Results take a week, by which time nobody cares
Paper mocks get checked over the weekend, rank lists are made in Excel, and by the time results are out the next test is due.

The test series doesn't feel like the real exam
Students need section timers, negative marking and an exam-style palette to build temperament. Google Forms gives them none of it.

Scholarship tests are a spreadsheet nightmare
Registrations come in from forms, WhatsApp and walk-ins, and nobody knows who actually wrote the test.

How it works for you

## Your exam cycle on Examezy

- Results on the same day as the test, not the next week
- A mock series that rehearses timing and negative marking
- Scholarship test registrants as verified, exportable leads
- Faculty teaching from question-level data

- 1 Build the paper Import past papers from Word, pick from your question bank or generate a chapter test with AI from your own notes.
- 2 Set it up like the real exam Physics, Chemistry and Maths sections with their own marks, negative marking, numeric-answer questions and a palette candidates already know.
- 3 Run it Students write at home or in your centre. Answers autosave; tab switches and camera checks keep it honest.
- 4 Publish rank and percentile instantly Release the moment the window closes. Every student sees rank, percentile, accuracy, time per section and how the class answered each question.
- 5 Teach from the data Question insights and the AI class diagnostic show which concepts the batch got wrong, so the next class starts from there.

## The parts coaching institutes use most
Online exams Exam-style sections, timers and palette. Results & analytics Rank, percentile and question insights within minutes. Open registration tests Scholarship tests with registration pages and automated reminders. AI question paper generator Chapter tests from your own material in minutes.
Popular use cases
Mock test series Scholarship & entrance tests Practice tests & homework

## Questions coaching institutes ask
Can't see yours? Ask us in the demo, or read the full FAQ .

Can I set JEE-style numeric-answer questions? +
Yes. Numeric questions accept integer or decimal answers, with more than one accepted value if needed, and are auto-marked.

Can students see their all-batch rank? +
Yes. Reports show rank and percentile among everyone who took the test, plus comparison with the class average and the topper.

Can I run the same test online for some students and on paper for others? +
Yes. Print the paper in shuffled sets for your centre, and run it online for students at home. Paper copies can be checked on screen or by AI, so results live in the same place.

Can parents get the result on WhatsApp? +
Result release can trigger WhatsApp messages through Automations, with rank and percentile.

Book a demo

For schools

# From unit test to pre-board, without the weekend of checking.
Most school exams are still written on paper, and that's fine. Examezy prints the paper, helps teachers check the copies on screen or with AI, and turns marks into report PDFs and class insights, with online quizzes for everything in between.
Book a demo See the workflow

Sound familiar?

## What gets in the way today
Teachers lose weekends to checking copies
A teacher with five sections and a 40-mark paper checks hundreds of copies every term, by hand, on top of teaching.

Marks live in registers, not in decisions
Nobody can see which chapter the whole grade struggled with until the report cards are already printed.

Parents want more than a number
A total out of 80 says little about what the child should practise next.

How it works for you

## Your exam cycle on Examezy

- Copies checked in hours instead of weekends
- A report PDF for every student, in one download
- Chapter-level insight before the next term starts
- Online quizzes and homework on the same platform

- 1 Set the paper Write it, import it from Word, or generate it with AI from your textbook with chapter weightage you choose.
- 2 Print it in sets Export multiple shuffled sets with roll number and invigilator fields, plus the answer key.
- 3 Scan the copies Scan the stack and upload it. AI matches each copy to the student by name and roll number.
- 4 Check on screen or with AI Teachers mark with pen and ticks on screen, or review AI-drafted marks and red-pen checked copies.
- 5 Share results Release results with a report PDF per student, and download every report in one ZIP for the PTM.

## The parts schools use most
Paper & offline exams Print shuffled sets and collect answer sheets as PDFs. AI answer-sheet checking AI drafts marks on handwritten copies; teachers approve. Results & analytics Report PDFs per student and question-level class insights. AI question paper generator Balanced papers from your textbook with page citations.
Popular use cases
School unit tests & term exams Practice tests & homework Olympiads & talent search

## Questions schools ask
Can't see yours? Ask us in the demo, or read the full FAQ .

Do our exams have to move online? +
No. Examezy is built for paper exams too: print the paper, scan the answer sheets, check them on screen or with AI, and publish results online.

Can AI check handwritten answers in our subjects? +
AI checking reads handwriting, including maths, and marks against a rubric. Every mark is a draft a teacher reviews. Try it on a few of your own copies in the demo.

Can we generate papers from NCERT books? +
Yes, AI paper generation works from your knowledge base, including textbooks, and cites the source page for each question.

Can parents see the report? +
Students can download their report PDF, and result release can trigger WhatsApp or email messages through Automations.

Book a demo

# Online Examination System for Colleges and Universities | Examezy
URL: https://examezy.com/for/colleges-universities/

- Home

For colleges & universities

# Internal assessments that run themselves, semester after semester.
Give every department one place to build question banks, run proctored internal tests, evaluate answer scripts on screen and see results by batch and evaluator, without a separate tool for each step.
Book a demo See the workflow

Follow up

- Ananya R. 3 tests missed
- Vivek P. Score down 22%
- Zoya K. Not started

Sound familiar?

## What gets in the way today
Every department runs exams differently
Some use forms, some use paper, some use the LMS quiz, and nobody can compare results across batches.

Evaluation is slow and hard to track
Answer scripts move between evaluators by hand, and the exam cell can't see what's checked and what's pending.

Integrity questions on online internals
Without proctoring, online internal marks are hard to defend.

How it works for you

## Your exam cycle on Examezy

- One exam workflow across departments
- An evaluation backlog the exam cell can see
- Proctored internals with reviewable evidence
- Batch and evaluator analytics every semester

- 1 Build shared banks Faculty contribute questions to an institute bank, tagged by subject and difficulty, reused across semesters.
- 2 Schedule internals Fixed windows, section timers, negative marking and random question order, assigned to batches.
- 3 Proctor online tests Full screen, tab-switch auto-submit and camera snapshots with a review timeline.
- 4 Evaluate with control Assign evaluators per assessment. They mark scripts on screen; the exam cell watches the backlog.
- 5 Analyse by batch and evaluator The dashboard shows score distributions, per-batch and per-evaluator statistics and students to follow up.

## The parts colleges & universities use most
AI proctoring Defensible online internals with snapshot timelines. Evaluation & marking On-screen evaluation and re-evaluation with access control. Question bank Shared banks across faculty and semesters. Results & analytics Department-wide dashboard and student reports.
Popular use cases
College internals & semester exams Campus & lateral hiring tests Surveys & feedback forms

## Questions colleges & universities ask
Can't see yours? Ask us in the demo, or read the full FAQ .

Can we control which faculty evaluate which exam? +
Yes. Each assessment's access settings decide who can edit it, who sees reports and who evaluates, by role or by named user.

Can students upload handwritten answer scripts? +
Yes. For remote written exams students upload one PDF; for hall exams the exam cell uploads scans.

Can we use it for course feedback surveys? +
Yes. Surveys are their own assessment type with a survey report of option percentages and free-text answers.

Can it run on our own domain and brand? +
Yes, Examezy runs on Vacademy's white-label portals with your domain and branding.

Book a demo

For hiring & HR teams

# Shortlist on skill, not on CVs.
Send one link to every applicant. They register, take a proctored aptitude and coding test, and you get a ranked shortlist with snapshot timelines the moment the window closes.
Book a demo See the workflow

Coding · Q2 · Two Sum · Python
Run
1 def two_sum(nums, target):
2 seen = {}
3 for i, n in enumerate(nums):
4 if target - n in seen:
5 return [seen[target - n], i]
6 seen[n] = i
7
Hidden tests

8 / 10 marks
8 of 10 test cases passed
Python JS C C++ Java Go

Sound familiar?

## What gets in the way today
Hundreds of CVs, no fair way to compare
Screening by CV favours keyword-stuffing. A short test tells you more in 40 minutes than a stack of resumes.

Unproctored tests invite help
Without basic checks, take-home tests measure who has the best friend.

Campus drives are chaos
Collecting registrations, sending links, chasing no-shows and building rank lists eats the HR team's week.

How it works for you

## Your exam cycle on Examezy

- A ranked shortlist the same day
- Evidence for every flagged attempt
- Campus drives without spreadsheet chaos
- Coding skill measured, not claimed

- 1 Open registration A public test page with your own fields: college, degree, graduation year, role applied for.
- 2 Build the round An aptitude MCQ section and a coding section, each with its own timer.
- 3 Proctor it Camera check-in, face checks, snapshots and auto-submit rules; full screen and tab-switch limits always on.
- 4 Shortlist Rank list with percentile and section scores, exported with your registration fields.
- 5 Review edge cases Open any attempt's proctoring timeline before you call the candidate.

## The parts hiring & hr teams use most
Coding tests Hidden test cases, six languages, proportional marks. AI proctoring Camera checks without video, auto-submit rules. Open registration tests One public link for every applicant. Results & analytics Rank lists and exports for the shortlist.
Popular use cases
Campus & lateral hiring tests Training & skill assessments

## Questions hiring & hr teams ask
Can't see yours? Ask us in the demo, or read the full FAQ .

Can candidates take the test without an account? +
Candidates register on your public page and verify by OTP, which gives you verified contact details for everyone who applied.

Which coding languages can candidates use? +
Python, JavaScript, C, C++, Java and Go.

Do you offer psychometric or personality tests? +
No. Examezy is for skill tests you author: aptitude, domain knowledge and coding.

Can we review a flagged candidate? +
Yes. Each attempt has a proctoring timeline with events and snapshots.

# Assessment Software for Training Institutes and Certification Bodies | Examezy
URL: https://examezy.com/for/training-certification/

- Home
- / Who it's for
- / Training & certification
For training & certification

# Assessments your certificates can stand on.
Whether you run vocational batches, professional courses or a certification programme, Examezy gives you proctored exams, section cutoffs, evaluator workflows and reports that make your results defensible.
Book a demo See the workflow

Proctoring · Riya Kapoor · attempt review
Flags 2 / 5
1 face on device
Faces are counted on the candidate's device. Snapshot every 60 s and at each flag. No video.

- 00:00 Camera check-in
- 12:41 Tab switch (1 of 3)
- 27:09 No face for 6 s
- 27:15 Face back in view
- 41:52 2 faces detected

Full screen enforced Copy & paste blocked Auto-submit after 5 flags

Sound familiar?

## What gets in the way today
Results need to be defensible
A certificate is only worth the assessment behind it. Unproctored, unaudited tests undermine the credential.

Practical and theory are assessed in different places
Objective theory in one tool, written answers on paper, scores in a spreadsheet.

Batches across cities
Trainers in different centres need the same paper, the same rules and one result sheet.

How it works for you

## Your exam cycle on Examezy

- One exam standard across every centre
- Reviewable proctoring evidence
- Theory and written answers in one result
- Reports ready to hand to candidates

- 1 Set the paper Sections with cutoff marks, negative marking and random order; objective and long-answer questions together.
- 2 Assign batches anywhere Same test for every centre, each with its own window if needed.
- 3 Proctor Browser rules plus camera checks with snapshot timelines.
- 4 Evaluate Auto-marking for objective parts; evaluators or AI for written answers, with release holds.
- 5 Report Per-candidate report PDFs and bulk ZIPs; automations notify candidates on release.

## The parts training & certification use most
AI proctoring Evidence trail for every attempt. Evaluation & marking Evaluator access and release holds. Online exams Sections with cutoffs and strict timing. Results & analytics Report PDFs per candidate.
Popular use cases
Training & skill assessments College internals & semester exams

## Questions training & certification ask
Can't see yours? Ask us in the demo, or read the full FAQ .

Does Examezy issue certificates? +
Not from the assessment itself. Examezy gives you scores, section cutoffs and report PDFs; certificates are issued from your course or your existing process.

Can I set a cutoff per section? +
Yes, each section can carry cutoff marks.

Is there a lockdown browser? +
No. Integrity comes from full-screen enforcement, tab-switch limits, camera checks and snapshot timelines.

Can trainers in different cities evaluate? +
Yes. Evaluator access is set per assessment, by role or named user, and evaluation happens in the browser.

Book a demo

## What gets in the way today
Building a test engine is a distraction
Timers, autosave, scale, marking rules, rank lists: it takes a year to build well and never stops needing work.

Learners compare you to the big platforms
Rank, percentile, detailed solutions and analytics are table stakes.

Content scales slower than demand
Writing thousands of quality questions takes time your team doesn't have.

How it works for you

- Re-engagement on autopilot

# How to Run an Online Mock Test Series (JEE, NEET, CUET, Banking) | Examezy
URL: https://examezy.com/use-cases/mock-test-series/

- Home
- / Use cases
- / Mock test series
Use case · Mock test series

# Mock test series that rehearse the real exam, not just the syllabus.
A mock is only useful if it feels like exam day and the analysis arrives while the student still remembers the paper. Here's the setup institutes use on Examezy.
Book a demo Jump to the setup

Leaderboard · All-India Mock 3 · 1,208 students
CSV · PDF

- 1 Kabir Singh 286/300 99.9
- 2 Ananya Rao 281/300 99.8
- 3 Mohd. Faiz 279/300 99.8
- 4 Ishita Das 274/300 99.7
- 5 Rohan Gupta 270/300 99.6
Percentile shown per student Report ZIP

The recipe

## How to set it up on Examezy

- 1 Choose the Mock type Mocks stay open with a fixed duration, so students can write when they're ready. Use the Exam type for a live all-batch mock in a fixed window.
- 2 Mirror the real paper's sections One section per subject, each with default marks and negative marking. Use numeric-answer questions where the real exam does.
- 3 Lock the timing Set one duration for the paper, or per-section timers if your exam has them, and turn on auto-submit at time-out.
- 4 Turn on integrity rules Full screen and tab-switch limits apply by default; add camera proctoring for all-India rank mocks.
- 5 Release instantly Release on submission for self-paced mocks, or at the end of the window for live rank lists.
- 6 Close the loop Students review every question with the explanation and see how the class answered; faculty use question insights for the next class.

Sample configuration
Assessment typeMock (self-paced) or Exam (live window)
SectionsPhysics · Chemistry · Maths (or your exam's pattern)
Marking+4 / −1 per section, numeric questions with exact answers
Timing180 min overall, auto-submit
OrderRandom question order within sections
ResultsRelease after the window ends

Tips from the field

- Publish the analysis the same day: the value of a mock halves with every day of delay.
- Add explanations to every question once; they serve every future batch.
- Use reattempts sparingly; the first attempt is the honest data point.
- Run a short practice set right after each mock on the chapters the batch got wrong.

## Questions
Popular with
Coaching institutes EdTech & test publishers

Can students retake a mock? +
You can grant reattempts per student from the monitoring console, and students can request one.

Can rank be calculated across centres? +
Yes. Everyone who takes the same assessment is ranked together with percentile, whether they wrote at home or in a centre.

What's the difference between Mock and Practice? +
Mocks have a fixed duration; Practice tests are untimed. Both stay available rather than running in a fixed window.

The recipe

## How to set it up on Examezy

- 1 Make the test public Turn on open registration and build the form: name, class, school, city, target exam.
- 2 Set two windows A registration window that runs for weeks, and an exam window on test day.
- 3 Automate reminders Registration confirmation, starting-soon and started messages by WhatsApp, email or push.

- Ask for the minimum the counsellor needs: every extra field lowers registrations.
- Share the link where your audience already is: school visits, WhatsApp groups, ads.
- Follow up within 48 hours of results, while the student is still excited.

# How Schools Run Unit Tests and Term Exams with Less Checking | Examezy

- / Use cases

Use case · School unit tests & term exams

# Keep the paper exam. Lose the paperwork.
Unit tests and term exams stay on paper, as they should. Examezy takes over everything around them: setting the paper, checking the copies and producing the reports.
Book a demo Jump to the setup

Evaluate · Class 10-B · Science term 1 · Roll 23
Draft saved

- Q3.Q4.3units missing1½
Marks

- Q1 2 / 2
- Q2 1 / 2
- Q3 3 / 3
- Q4 1.5 / 3
- Q5 — / 5
Total 7.5 / 15
Submit & release

The recipe

## How to set it up on Examezy

- 1 Set the paper Generate it from the textbook with chapter weightage, or import last year's paper from Word.
- 2 Print sets Export two or more shuffled sets with roll-number fields and an answer key.
- 3 Scan and upload Scan the copies and bulk upload them; AI matches each copy to the student.
- 4 Check Teachers check on screen, or approve AI-drafted marks on red-pen checked copies.
- 5 Release and report Release results; download every student's report PDF in one ZIP for the PTM.

Sample configuration
Assessment typePaper exam with uploaded answer sheets
PaperSets A and B, shuffled, answer key
EvaluationAI checking on, teacher review before release
ResultsReleased manually after review
ReportsBulk ZIP, one PDF per student

Tips from the field

- Scan at 200–300 dpi in black and white for the most reliable reading.
- Ask students to write name and roll number clearly on the first page: matching depends on it.
- Write a model answer for long questions; AI marking follows it closely.

## Questions
Popular with
Schools

Can AI check every subject? +
AI checking reads handwriting, including maths, and marks against a rubric per question. Try it on your own copies in the demo; teachers always approve the marks.

What if a copy can't be matched to a student? +
It waits for a teacher to pick the student. The AI never guesses.

Can we run online quizzes too? +
Yes. Practice tests and homework run online on the same platform.

# How to Run Online Campus Hiring and Lateral Hiring Tests | Examezy
URL: https://examezy.com/use-cases/campus-hiring-tests/

- Home
- / Use cases
- / Campus & lateral hiring tests
Use case · Campus & lateral hiring tests

# From 2,000 applicants to a 50-person shortlist in an afternoon.
A two-section online test, aptitude and coding, filters a campus drive faster and more fairly than any CV screen. Here's the setup.
Book a demo Jump to the setup

Coding · Q2 · Two Sum · Python
Run
1 def two_sum(nums, target):
2 seen = {}
3 for i, n in enumerate(nums):
4 if target - n in seen:
5 return [seen[target - n], i]
6 seen[n] = i
7
Hidden tests

8 / 10 marks
8 of 10 test cases passed
Python JS C C++ Java Go

The recipe

## How to set it up on Examezy

- 1 Registration page College, degree, year, role. Share one link with every placement cell.
- 2 Two sections Aptitude MCQs (30 min) and coding (60 min), switching locked.
- 3 Proctoring Camera mandatory to start, auto-submit after 5 flags.
- 4 Fixed window Everyone writes in the same window; results released at the end.
- 5 Shortlist Sort by section scores and percentile; export with registration fields.
- 6 Check before calling Open the proctoring timeline of each shortlisted candidate.

Sample configuration
Assessment typeExam, public
SectionsAptitude (MCQ, 30 min) · Coding (2 problems, 60 min)
Coding languagesPython, JavaScript, C, C++, Java, Go
ProctoringCamera required, auto-submit after 5 flags
ResultsReleased after window; rank list export

Tips from the field

- Use two medium coding problems rather than one hard one: partial marks separate candidates better.
- Lock section switching so aptitude time can't be borrowed for coding.
- Generate a fresh coding set per drive with AI to avoid leaked questions.

## Questions
Popular with
Hiring & HR teams Colleges & universities

Can we send different tests to different roles? +
Yes. Create one assessment per role, each with its own registration page.

Do candidates need to install anything? +
No, everything runs in the browser.

Can we detect copied code? +
Not across candidates today; integrity comes from proctoring and shuffled order.

# Examezy vs Google Forms for Online Exams: An Honest Comparison | Examezy
URL: https://examezy.com/compare/google-forms/

- Home
- / Compare
- / Examezy vs Google Forms
Compare

# Google Forms is a great form. Your exam deserves an exam platform.
Plenty of institutes start their online exams on Google Forms, and for a five-question class quiz it's fine. Here's an honest look at what changes when the exam matters.

What matters | Examezy | Google Forms |

Timer and auto-submit | Per test, section or question; auto-submit at time-out | No built-in timer (add-ons only) |
Sections with own marks and negative marking | Yes, per section | Points per question; no negative marking |
Question types | MCQ single/multiple, true/false, numeric, one word, long answer, coding, passage-based | Choice, checkbox, short and paragraph text, grids |
Integrity | Full screen, tab-switch auto-submit, camera checks with snapshots | Locked mode only on managed Chromebooks |
Dropped connection | Answers kept on the device and synced; attempts resumable | Progress is saved only for respondents signed in to Google |
Rank and percentile | Automatic, in every student's report | Not available; export to Sheets and build it |
Written / handwritten answers | On-screen checking with pen tools, AI checking | Read typed text yourself; file uploads need a Google sign-in |
Question bank | Searchable bank, reuse across tests, AI generation | Copy forms or import questions manually |
Reports | Student report PDFs, question insights, bulk ZIP, AI diagnostics | Summary charts per question |
Price | Paid plans sized to your exams | Free |

Based on publicly documented features as of October 2026. Tell us if something has changed.
Stick with Google Forms when…

- Quick, low-stakes class polls and quizzes
- You need something in five minutes and results don't need ranks
- Every student uses a school-managed Chromebook and you only need locked mode

Move to Examezy when…

- Exams with timers, sections and negative marking
- Results that need rank, percentile and analysis
- Proctoring for anything that counts
- Written answers that need checking
- A question bank you reuse every term
Book a demo

## Where Google Forms works well
Forms is free, everyone knows it, and it's quick for a short check-for-understanding quiz. If that's all you need, keep using it.

## Where it starts to hurt
Real exams need a clock, sections, negative marking and fair conditions, and the result needs to mean something to the student: rank, percentile, which questions to revisit. Forms has none of this built in, so institutes bolt on timers, spreadsheets and manual rank lists, and the work moves to the teacher.

## What changes on Examezy
The exam behaves like the real one, the answers survive a bad connection, proctoring rules apply automatically, objective marks arrive instantly and written answers are checked on screen or by AI. Every student gets a report, and you get the class picture.

## Questions
Can I import my Google Forms quizzes? +
Export your questions to a Word document and import them with markers, or paste them and let AI structure the paper.

Is Examezy free like Google Forms? +
No. Examezy is a paid platform sized to your exam volume. Book a demo for a quote; we can start with a pilot exam.

Book a 30-minute demo. Send us a past paper beforehand and we'll show it running as an Examezy test: proctored, auto-marked and reported.

# How to Conduct an Online Exam: A 12-Step Checklist for Institutes | Examezy
URL: https://examezy.com/blog/how-to-conduct-online-exam/

- Home
- / Blog
- / How to Conduct an Online Exam: A 12-Step Checklist for Institutes
Guides

# How to Conduct an Online Exam: A 12-Step Checklist for Institutes
A practical checklist for conducting online exams: choosing the format, building the paper, timing, marking rules, proctoring, a dry run, exam-day monitoring, evaluation and publishing results.
By the Examezy team · 15 October 2026· 8 min read

## Key takeaways

- Decide the format (live window, self-paced mock or practice) before you write a single question.
- Mirror the real exam's sections, timing and marking so the result means something.
- Run a dry run with five people a week before: it catches 90% of exam-day problems.
- Plan the evaluation and result release up front, not after the exam closes.

## Before the exam: decide the format
Most online exam problems are decided long before exam day. The first choice is the format. A live exam runs in a fixed window, and everyone writes at the same time; this is right for internals, scholarship tests and anything ranked. A self-paced mock stays open with a fixed duration, which suits test series. A practice test is untimed and exists to teach, not to rank.
Write the format down along with who is taking it, how results will be used, and who checks any written answers. Those four lines answer most of the questions your team will ask later.

## The 12-step checklist

- Fix the format: live window, self-paced mock or practice.
- Build the paper from your question bank, an imported Word file or an AI draft you have reviewed.
- Split it into sections that mirror the real exam, each with its own marks and negative marking.
- Choose timing: one duration, per-section timers, or per-question timers, and whether time-out submits automatically.
- Decide question order: shuffle within sections so neighbours see different orders.
- Pick integrity rules: full screen and tab-switch limits at minimum; camera checks for anything ranked or certified.
- Write the instructions: how long, how many sections, what happens on a tab switch, what to do if the internet drops.
- Assign candidates by batch, or open a registration page for public tests.
- Schedule reminders for the day before and an hour before.
- Run a dry run with five people on different devices and networks.
- On exam day, watch the Ongoing and Pending lists and remind no-shows.
- Evaluate, review and release results on the schedule you announced.

## Why the dry run matters
A dry run with a handful of colleagues on phones, old laptops and patchy Wi-Fi will surface instruction gaps, wrong answer keys and timing mistakes while they are still cheap to fix. Ask each tester to switch tabs once and to turn their Wi-Fi off for thirty seconds, so you know exactly what candidates will see.

## On exam day
Keep one person on monitoring and one on candidate support. Most support requests are about camera permission, a browser that isn't up to date, or a candidate who started late. Have a short written answer ready for each.

- Open the monitoring console 15 minutes before start.
- Send a reminder to anyone in Pending five minutes after start.
- Log every exception (a granted reattempt, a technical issue) in one place.

## After the exam: evaluation and results
Objective questions should be marked the moment the exam ends. For written answers, decide in advance who evaluates and by when. If you use AI to draft marks, budget time for teachers to review before release.
Publish when you said you would. A result that arrives the same day is a learning moment; one that arrives two weeks later is just a number.

Where Examezy fits
Examezy covers every step above in one place: sections, timers, negative marking, shuffled order, full-screen and tab-switch rules, camera proctoring, batch or public registration, a live monitoring console, auto-marking, on-screen and AI evaluation, and release on your schedule.

Book a demo

## Frequently asked questions
How long should an online exam be? +
Match the real exam if you're rehearsing for one. For internal tests, 45 to 90 minutes keeps attention and limits connection risk.

What if a student's internet drops? +
Use a platform that saves answers on the device and syncs them, and tell students in the instructions what they'll see if the connection drops.

- After the exam: evaluation and results

# Online Exam Proctoring: What Works, What Doesn't, and What It Costs Candidates | Examezy
URL: https://examezy.com/blog/online-exam-proctoring-guide/

- Home
- / Blog
- / Online Exam Proctoring: What Works, What Doesn't, and What It Costs Candidates
Proctoring

# Online Exam Proctoring: What Works, What Doesn't, and What It Costs Candidates
An honest guide to online proctoring methods (browser rules, camera snapshots, AI face detection, live invigilators, lockdown browsers): what each catches, its cost to candidates, and how to choose.
By the Examezy team · 15 October 2026· 8 min read

## Key takeaways

- Proctoring is a deterrent first and a detector second; visible rules prevent most cheating.
- Every method has a cost: bandwidth, privacy, installation friction or human time.
- Match the method to the stakes: practice tests need none, ranked exams need browser rules and camera checks.
- Decide what a flag means before the exam, not after.

## The main proctoring methods
Method | What it catches | Cost to candidates |

Browser rules (full screen, tab-switch limits, copy blocked) | Searching answers in another tab, copy-paste | Almost none |
Camera snapshots | Someone else writing, a second person in the room | Camera permission; little bandwidth |
On-device face detection | No face or multiple faces, in real time | Camera permission; runs locally |
Continuous video recording | Most visible behaviour, for later review | High bandwidth, privacy concerns, review hours |
Live human invigilators | Behaviour in real time, with judgement | Scheduling, cost, stable video connection |
Lockdown browsers | Other apps and tabs entirely | Installation, device compatibility issues |

No method catches everything. A phone below the camera's view defeats most of them. That's why proctoring works best as a visible deterrent combined with question design that makes copying less useful: shuffled order, application questions and a time limit that leaves no room to search.

## Match the method to the stakes

- Practice and homework: no proctoring. The point is learning.
- Weekly tests and mocks: browser rules, with tab-switch auto-submit.
- Ranked mocks, scholarship tests, internals: browser rules plus camera snapshots and face checks.
- Certification and hiring: the above, with a camera required to start and a clear violation limit.

## Decide what a flag means
A flag isn't proof. Cameras lose focus, siblings walk past, Wi-Fi drops. Decide in advance whether flags auto-submit after a limit or only get recorded for a human to judge, and say so in the instructions. Candidates behave better when they know the rules, and you avoid arguments later.
When you review, look at the timeline: one 'no face' event during a 90-minute exam is noise; a cluster of tab switches followed by a jump in correct answers deserves a conversation.

## Privacy is part of fairness
Streaming video from a teenager's bedroom is a big ask. Methods that run detection on the candidate's device and upload only occasional stills collect far less, which is easier to justify to parents and easier to store responsibly.

Where Examezy fits
Examezy's proctoring is deliberately light: full screen, tab-switch warnings with auto-submit on the third switch, copy and paste blocked, and optional camera proctoring that counts faces on the candidate's device and uploads small snapshots, never video. You choose auto-submit after 3, 5 or 10 flags, or record only.
It doesn't offer a lockdown browser, ID matching or live invigilators. If you need those, we'll tell you so in the demo.

Book a demo

## Frequently asked questions
Can online proctoring detect a phone? +
Most camera-based methods can't reliably see a phone held below the camera. Use time limits and application questions to reduce what a phone can help with.

Is AI proctoring legal in India? +
Collecting images of candidates is personal data processing. Tell candidates what you collect and why, collect the minimum, and follow your institution's data policy.

On this page

- The main proctoring methods
- Match the method to the stakes
- Decide what a flag means
- Privacy is part of fairness

# Negative Marking Explained: How to Set It and When Not To | Examezy
URL: https://examezy.com/blog/negative-marking-explained/

- Home
- / Blog
- / Negative Marking Explained: How to Set It and When Not To
Question papers

# Negative Marking Explained: How to Set It and When Not To
What negative marking is, how common schemes like +4/−1 and +1/−0.25 work, the maths of guessing, and when negative marking helps or hurts your test.
By the Examezy team · 15 October 2026· 6 min read

## Key takeaways

- Negative marking deducts marks for wrong answers to discourage blind guessing.
- With 4 options, a penalty of one-third of the marks makes a blind guess worth zero on average.
- Use it when your real exam does, so students practise the decision to skip.
- Leave it off for practice tests where you want students to attempt everything.

## What negative marking is
Negative marking takes marks away for a wrong answer and gives zero for a question left blank. It exists to make guessing a decision rather than a free lottery ticket.

## The maths of guessing
Take a 4-option MCQ worth +4 with a −1 penalty. A blind guess is right one time in four: the expected score is (¼ × 4) + (¾ × −1) = +0.25 per question. A small positive edge. If the student can eliminate one option, the odds become one in three: (⅓ × 4) + (⅔ × −1) = +0.67. Eliminating two options makes it +1.5.
For a +1 / −0.25 scheme with 4 options, a blind guess is worth (¼ × 1) + (¾ × −0.25) ≈ +0.06: close to neutral. To make it exactly zero, the penalty has to be one-third of the marks (−0.33 on a 1-mark question), because the three wrong options must cancel the one right one.
Expected marks per question attempted, by marking scheme.Scheme | Options | Blind guess (expected) | After eliminating one option |

+4 / −1 | 4 | +0.25 | +0.67 |
+1 / −0.25 | 4 | +0.06 | +0.17 |
+1 / −0.33 | 4 | 0.00 | +0.11 |
+2 / −0.5 | 4 | +0.13 | +0.33 |

## When to use it, and when not to

- Use it in mocks for exams that have it, so students practise the skip-or-attempt decision under time pressure.
- Use it in ranked tests where lucky guesses would distort the rank list.
- Skip it in practice tests and homework: you want every question attempted so you can see what they don't know.
- Skip it for questions with many possible answers (numeric, one word) unless the real exam penalises them.

## Teach the strategy, not just the rule
The best use of negative marking in a mock is the analysis afterwards: how many marks did the student lose to wrong attempts, and in which section? A student losing 20 marks to guesses in one subject has a different problem from one who leaves 15 questions blank.

Where Examezy fits
On Examezy, negative marking is set per section, alongside default marks, cutoffs and question order, and every student's report shows marks gained and lost, accuracy and time by section.

Book a demo

- The maths of guessing
- When to use it, and when not to
- Teach the strategy, not just the rule
